# Phase directive — «A fired scheduled wake keeps the wheel» (Epoch 4, viola-0.2.0; the head entry at `33321186`)

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. Nothing else under it is read, cited or snapped. A fact the
plan needs and this directive does not state is ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

The operator is AWAY from this session (he answers through the overseers' dialogs): raise NO question dialog for
him. A fork that is his is written to `{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the options in order with each
one's cost, the recommendation marked) and the step stops there, saying so. A technical fork is answered by the
overseer's relay at once. **This phase makes NO live start and reads nothing of the operator's real `~/.claude*`.**
In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## Facts, measured by the overseer 2026-11-19 — cite them as this directive's

- A bare `claude` on this host is 2.1.328 (`~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.328/claude`); this builder runs
  it. The tree at `33321186` holds 25 relied ledger rows (the 25th, `local-command-context`, landed today); the
  live home's stamp is 24 rows and the pinned product (the release build of `a59da9da`) that drives this session
  is untouched until its re-pin. A stamp of 25 rows for 2.1.328 stands only in the rig's kept scratch stamp
  (`target/live-rig/context-stamp.json`, gitignored local state).
- This very session is driven through the product, and the defect this entry mends is why it is told to set no
  scheduled wake: a fired wake's prompt is filed `origin: human`, the wheel goes to `human`, and every driver send
  is refused until a release. That rule stands for THIS phase too: call no scheduled-wake or timer tool.
- The rig's `SF` arm runs inside a `bwrap` sandbox; its kept dirs are keyed by the CLI version; a live arm that
  needs a verified CLI is seeded from a kept stamp of the rig's own verify (`CS` → `CC` today).
- The documentation leaves hold no figure the code states: this chunk adds none.
- The operator is asleep until the morning: a fork of his WAITS in `founder-forks.md`. Nothing that needs his
  word is planned around.

## The directive

1. Scope is the route entry and its carries as they stand at `33321186`, nothing wider: a CLI-scheduled wake's
   prompt told from a typed one, the driver keeping its sends and dialogs (the capability the entry names); the
   hint's cell attribute (a third reading: a fresh box, keys before any send, a start that makes no send after
   them); the intermittent rehearsal red (acted on only at its next red); the boot-timeout WATCH (read at each
   run, no bound moved). Every carry is disposed by name in the plan.
2. **The size risk is the MEANS.** The entry leaves it to this phase: the CLI sends no field (read live on three
   starts, the carry holds the readings). Say at P3, from the code and from what can be read with NO start (the
   installed 2.1.328 bundle, the wrapper's byte-source and wheel code, the earlier chunks' evidence in the
   store):
   - each candidate means, what it rests on, and how it FAILS — the carry's hypothesis (the wrapper owns the
     pty and knows no byte came from the human's side before the prompt was submitted while a wake was
     scheduled) among them, and any other the code offers (the turn end's `scheduled_wakes` count, a
     transcript read, a hook the CLI fires for a wake);
   - for each, the FALSE POSITIVE that matters most: a prompt the HUMAN typed that would be told as a wake —
     the driver then sends over a human at the keyboard. Say exactly which human acts each means can and cannot
     tell apart (a paste, a key during the wake's fire, a prompt typed while a wake is pending, a second wrapper
     or a resumed session), and what the product does when it cannot tell: the conservative side is `human`;
   - what the wheel, the send path and a held dialog do after a wake is told as one, and what an older CLI or
     an unverified one gets;
   - whether a ledger row with a verify probe is part of it (a wake must then be SCHEDULED and FIRED inside
     verify: how long that takes, what it types, what it leaves) or the capability rests on another proof —
     and what a new relied row would again do to every stamped version;
   - whether one implement window holds it, or the entry splits and where.
3. **At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block in `founder-forks.md`:** your window; the means recommended and
   the ones set aside, each with its false positive; the split or no split; every live start's SHAPE before the
   count — processes, every byte typed, how the wake is scheduled and how long until it fires, the stop, every
   file written and where, under WHICH home; for each start a predicate its reading can FAIL, the red reading
   named; what each start READS (key names, counts, closed words, cell attributes — never a text) and whether
   any of it is a reading or a typed literal no row yet names — a widening is said as one HERE, not at P4;
   whether any typed key moves the wheel before a send; the capability's concretized claim and what «verified»
   would rest on; a recommended cap and what one spare would be for; the keys the hint reading needs. The cap,
   the keys, any widening, what «verified» rests on and any read or write under his real home are the
   founder's: the block WAITS for him.
4. **For every capped start, name what it needs ABSENT or PRESENT on disk outside the tree** (a kept stamp, a
   kept dir, a scratch, a runtime dir), each with a no-start gate entry right before the start, placed so a
   round resumed at one entry still fires it; a start whose product is kept gets an entry that reads it AFTER.
5. One ledger, one count: `--cap` is the RUNNING total of base starts in the ledger file (the first start's
   entry `--cap 1`, the second's `--cap 2`). A census entry after the LAST live leg is keyed to the operator leg.
6. Every control stands on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases AND building the whole workspace where the
   case needs a root binary; its `--timeout S` named and passed, ids within 16 characters. Every filter term of
   a gate entry SELECTS at least one test under its layer flag. An expect atom must be able to fail; a word that
   may honestly read two ways is a READING recorded, not a failing atom. A test that skips prints its reason.
7. Before a live round the host is read (`hostwatch.py read --last 15`): a CONTENDED reading with a NEIGHBOUR
   named stops and is re-read, never retried into. The token window is the rig's own check, never a hand read;
   a start refused for it is uncounted — stop and say so.
8. No mutation run. A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint — a rehearsal of a wake does not sleep
   out a real schedule. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home. Read `df` before a whole rebuild.
9. A fold is decided at the PHASE. A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop
   and tell the overseer. On an account-limit refusal, stop where you are.
10. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool, with any argument. End every process you start.
11. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the
    union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY cited row is in the union or its standing
    list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` /
    `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

   - `Observed<R>::read` calls a new `WheelSlot::human_key()` in place of `human_input()`. Under the one `held` lock it
     sets `typed = true`, then makes the `Input::Human` move. The non-editing list and the classifier are unchanged
     (security · decision/non-editing-list-measured-only).
   - `human_input()` stays for the hook path and sets no mark.
   - No log line, span or event is added: the mark is in-memory wrapper state (architecture ·
     decision/wheel-in-wrapper-memory).

2. `WheelSlot` gains three methods:
   - `take_typed() -> bool`: reads `typed` and clears it.
   - `count_wakes(Option<u64>)`: sets `wakes`.
   - `wakes() -> Option<u64>`.

   Each is a short `held`-lock section. The hook path calls them under the flight lock, flight before held, as
   `append_hook_event` already orders them (`src/run/send/slot.rs:222-255`).

3. In `append_hook_event`, under the flight guard, for a `turn-ended` line: `slot.wheel.count_wakes(the line's
   scheduled_wakes as u64, None when null)`. A `session-start` or `session-end` sets `None`, since a new session holds
   none of the old crons. An API-error turn end reads `null` and so sets `None`.

4. For a `prompt-submitted` the in-flight send did not claim and the hook filed `human`, under the same guard:
   - Read `typed = slot.wheel.take_typed()`.
   - **Told as a wake** when `!typed && slot.wheel.wakes().is_some_and(|n| n >= 1) && slot.cli_verified`:
     `line.data["origin"] = "harness"` and NO `human_input()`.
   - **Otherwise:** `human_input()`, as today.

   The relabel is made before the line can be read, as the driver relabel is. A driver-claimed or hook-`harness`
   prompt neither reads nor clears the mark. The doc comment on `append_hook_event` states the rule in these words.

5. **Where the mark clears (`inputs#I3` item 6):** only when a human-filed prompt is appended, whether told human or
   told as a wake. It does NOT clear at a turn end, at a `release`, or at a driver or harness prompt.
   - So a message the human typed during a running turn and the CLI submitted after that turn's end still reads
     human: its byte set the mark, and nothing cleared it.
   - That stays true when a `viola release` came between. `release` clearing the mark is the one remaining door to
     the founder's named false positive. This plan leaves that door closed, and a case pins it closed (step 10).
   - The cost: a draft the human typed and erased with no prompt keeps the mark, and the next fired wake reads human
     (today's behaviour, once). That is the conservative side.
   - The mouse-only submit stays the named unmeasured false positive (`inputs#I3` item 1).

6. Append `LedgerRow::StopSessionCrons` LAST to the enum and to `ALL` (`[Self; 26]`):
   - id `stop-session-crons`;
   - words `Stop carries session_crons as an array`;
   - `check`: the run the `StopMessage` arm reads (`run.first(HookEvent::Stop)`), `is_some_and(|p|
     p["session_crons"].is_array())`.
   - `row_word` unchanged: a missing or non-array key reads `fail`, never `absent`. The shape is read in this crate
     alone (architecture · decision/cli-capability-ledger); no element is read (security ·
     decision/stop-session-crons-count-only).
   - Verify gains no run, paste, wait or step of its own. Its step line `[26/26] stop-session-crons …` comes from
     `relied()`'s count (design history, 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows).

7. **The count pins move 25 → 26,** with `stop-session-crons` appended last wherever a list of ids is pinned. The
   retired-shape sweep (`command grep -rlE '/25\]|25/25|\[25/|; 25\]|ALL.len\(\), 25|twenty-five|25 pass' --include=*.rs .`
   at `33321186`: 8 files) finds:
   - `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` and `ledger/test_cases_stamps.rs`;
   - `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` (`LEDGER_ROWS`);
   - `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`;
   - `src/cmd/verify.rs`, `src/run/version_gate.rs`;
   - `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`.

   It also reads every `len()` assertion in the files the relied set feeds (testing.md 2026-11-19):
   `tests/cli_verify/runs.rs`, `tests/support/verify.rs`, `tests/support/home.rs`,
   `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs`. Implement re-runs the sweep after
   the move, and only a hit that IS the relied-row count moves.

   `FLOOR_ROWS` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs:76`) takes `stop-session-crons` exactly as `stop-message` stands in
   it. Both read the same Stop capture, so the new row joins it and the array becomes `[&str; 22]`. Its doc pin moves
   with it.

8. `--stop-crons <n>` (argv-only, 0-4): every Stop the fake fires carries `session_crons` as an array of `n` synthetic
   elements, each the object `{"synthetic":true}`. With no option, the recorded payload's own `session_crons` stands

     set moves.

     and the `STAMPED` list unmoved (`inputs#I3` item 9).

9. `--wake-after-ms <ms>` (argv-only, at most 5 000): once, that many ms after the first Stop that carried a non-empty
   `session_crons`, the fake fires one keyless `UserPromptSubmit` of the recorded default prompt, then, under
   `--turn-stop`, its Stop. No byte is read from stdin for it. It is the rig rehearsal's stand-in for the CLI's own
   fire.

   The root cases fire their keyless prompt by a scripted `UserPromptSubmit` step, as `--inject-harness-turn`'s
   precedent does (test-plan · contract/fake-script/format, unchanged).

body:
11. **Root integration cases** in `tests/cli_wheel.rs` (the `stamped_home` fixture, a copy of the recorded set with the
    fake's `--stop-crons 1 --turn-stop` and a script):
    - `path5_a_fired_wake_keeps_the_driver_wheel_its_next_send_and_its_dialog`:
      - a driver send whose turn ends with one wake counted, then a scripted keyless `UserPromptSubmit`;
      - its `prompt-submitted` reads `origin:"harness"`, and no `wheel` line follows the start record;
      - after its Stop, a second driver send exits 0 confirmed;
      - a scripted question dialog is held (`dialog_pending` true) and answered by `viola answer`, exit 0.
    - `path5_a_keyless_prompt_with_no_wake_counted_takes_the_wheel` (`--stop-crons 0`): `origin:"human"`,
      `wheel{human,human-input}`, the next send exit 10.
    - `path5_a_fired_wake_on_an_unverified_cli_takes_the_wheel` (`StampedHome::unstamped`): `origin:"human"`, the
      wheel human.

12. **E2E cases** in `tests/tui_wheel.rs` (outer-PTY steps, as its harness-turn case):
    - `tui_a_human_key_before_a_fired_wake_takes_the_wheel`: one key typed, then `viola release`, then the turn ends
      with one wake counted, then the keyless prompt. It reads `origin:"human"` and a `wheel{human,human-input}` line
      after the release.
    - `tui_a_message_queued_during_a_turn_reads_human_after_that_turn_ends` (the overseer's FP rehearsal, `inputs#I3`
      item 6): a human byte during a running turn, the prompt submitted after that turn's end with one wake counted. It
      reads exactly what the product does: `origin:"human"`, the wheel human. Its sibling `…_and_a_release_between` adds
      `viola release` before the submit and reads the same.

13. **The ledger row's unit cases** in `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_checks.rs`: a Stop with an
    empty array reads pass; absent, `null`, a string or an object read fail. In `test_cases_stamps.rs`: a stamp of the
    25 earlier ids reads unverified, and 26 passing ids read verified.

14. **Labels.** `of_label` gains:
    - `WS` → `Arm::V`, with the stamp shape;
    - `HB` and `HB-2` → a new `Arm::HB`;
    - `R3W` and `R3W-2` → `Arm::R3`, with the seeded shape.

    `ContextShape` becomes the kept-stamp shape, carrying its file: `CS`/`CC` keep and seed `context-stamp.json`; `WS`
    keeps and `R3W` seeds `wake-stamp.json`. The S1/S2 names the founder used are not rig labels: `S1`/`S2` already
    name `TS`/`TC`. A `-2` label counts against `--spare` alone (`ledger::admit`).

15. **`WS`** is `CS`'s shape under its own file: verify into the scratch viola home, the stamp copied through
    `place_private_new` to `<out>/wake-stamp.json`, never over a standing file (`kept-stamp: written · exists · absent ·
    refused`), and `config-top:` read as `CS` reads it.

17. **`R3W`** (`arm_r3` under the seeded shape):
    - `<out>/wake-stamp.json` is copied into the scratch viola home's `ledger/stamps.json` before `viola run`
      (`stamp-seeded: yes · absent · refused`; absent or refused is `refused: stamp`, uncounted);
    - send 1 `Wake::Interval.text(true)`, the stand to `--stand`, the fired turn's end, as today's R3.

    After the fired turn ends:
    - `wheel-after-fire: kept · human · other · unread` — read from the scratch events log's `wheel` lines past send 1's
      `prompt-submitted` offset (`kept` when there are none), reading each start's own lines from its own offset
      (test-plan history, 2026-11-15);
    - `wake-origin` (today's word, `harness` now expected);
    - send 2 `PLAIN_TEXT` (`send-2-reply: <word>`).

    This is the reading of viola's OWN `wheel` lines and origin word, in the width the founder ratified with `S3`
    (`inputs#I3` item 3). No key is typed.
18. **`screen.rs`:** no change. `hint_cells` and `box_attr` serve `HB` as they stand.

title: H. The live round (operator-attended, founder-capped: `WS`, `HB`, `R3W`, ONE spare; `inputs#I3` items 3, 7, 8)

data.head: ### H. The live round (operator-attended, founder-capped: `WS`, `HB`, `R3W`, ONE spare; `inputs#I3` items 3, 7, 8)

body:
20. Fired through `gate.py run --live-legs`, in block order:
    - the install read by path, the census, the plain build and hash;
    - the live home stamps' sha (before);
    - then, per start: a host read, the scratch base read empty, the start's own absence read, the start, the census,
      and the live home sha (unmoved).

    The order is `WS` (`--cap 1`), then `HB` (`--cap 2`), then `R3W` (`--cap 3`); `R3W` reads `wake-stamp.json`
    PRESENT first. Every start passes `--spare 1`. The operator-keyed census and sha come after the last leg. A host
    read reading CONTENDED with a NEIGHBOUR named stops and is re-read, never retried into. The token window is the
    rig's own check: a start refused for it is uncounted, and the round stops and says so.

21. **Reds.**
    - `HB`'s `hint-cells: unread (no-cell)` on a fresh box is a red of that start's premise alone. It stops nothing
      else: the round goes on to `R3W`, fired by `--entry` where the round tool stops on a red.
    - `R3W`'s fail words are stopping reds.

22. **The spare** (`HB-2` or `R3W-2`, at most one) is fired only in two cases, never on a red reading:
    - for `R3W` when the wake did not fire inside `--stand 300` (`wake: unfired`); the CLI's interval wake is expected
      about 60 s after send 1's turn, and the stand bound is 300 s;
    - for `HB` when the box is not up at the first frame (`refused: shape`, uncounted already, so the spare is kept for
      `R3W`).

    Unfired, it is recorded `not fired — spare unspent`. A fourth base start is the founder's alone.

23. As the block's operator entries say: pre-push, hygiene, the pre-CI commit (the operator's), the clean-tree push and
    the CI read.
- none
- `src/run/wheel.rs` — the `typed` mark and `wakes` count in `Held`, `human_key`, `take_typed`, `count_wakes`, `wakes`, its unit cases
- `src/run/send/slot.rs` — the told-wake rule and the wake count in `append_hook_event`
- `src/run/send/relabel.rs` — the keyless-prompt rule table
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — `LedgerRow::StopSessionCrons`, `ALL` at 26
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_checks.rs` — the row's check cases

- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — `step_line` pins at /26
- `src/run/version_gate.rs` — the stamps-verdict ladder at 26
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — `--stop-crons`, `--wake-after-ms`
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — `LEDGER_ROWS` and its stdout pin
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — labels, the kept-stamp shape, `HB`, `FLOOR_ROWS`
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/wake.rs` — `R3W`'s seeding, `wheel-after-fire`, send 2
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` — the label help text
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the `ws`, `hb`, `r3w` rehearsals and the 26 pin
- `tests/cli_wheel.rs` — the three Path 5 wake cases
- `tests/tui_wheel.rs` — the key-before-wake case and the two queued-message cases
- `tests/cli_verify.rs` — the all-pass stdout at 26
- `tests/cli_verify/runs.rs` — its relied-count pins, read at implement
- `tests/support/verify.rs` — the stamped-home rows
- `tests/support/home.rs` — the stamped home's relied rows

The block runs, in order:
- the formatter, the linter and the agent crate's unit cases;
- the workspace unit layer;
- the integration binaries the wheel and the count pins reach;
- the E2E binaries (the outer-PTY wheel cases and the ledger contracts);
- the rig rehearsals and the rig's inline cases;
- the live round (§H);
- the whole integration and E2E layers;
- the operator pass.
**What is not run, and why:**

- No smoke entry. The boot-path reach is the harness boot's stamping `viola verify`, whose relied count moves. Every
  stamped harness session in the E2E layer fires it (`run --e2e`), and `binary(cli_verify)` runs that verify over the
  fake. `src/run/version_gate.rs` moves test pins only.
- No release check: the product graph gains no dependency, and the fake and rig are test-only.
- No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 8).
**Bounds:**
- The root and E2E cases wait on events lines under `WITHIN` (12 s), with no sleep.
- The rehearsals run under `--deadline 15`. `r3w`'s `--stand 6` is the fake's fire at 1 s plus the turn.

- Live: `WS` `--deadline 1200`, as `CS`. `HB` `--deadline 300`: one frame and two keys. `R3W` `--deadline 900` with
  `--stand 300`: about 60 s to the fire, three model turns.
**Homes:**
- Every test runs under its own home and a test-owned user home.
- The live starts run under the rig's scratch at `/tmp/viola-rig-<uid>/` and its private config.

- From the real home: the credentials file is read once per start (a 0600 copy, removed at teardown) and
  `~/.claude.json` is stamped read-only. Nothing is written under `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`.
  `~/.viola/ledger/stamps.json` is hashed only (`inputs#I3` item 3).

**The live legs' non-priming probes** are the round entries before each start: the install read, the census, the build
hash, the host read, the scratch base read, and the start's absence read. Kept frames go to a per-start
`<pid>-<ms>/` dir under `target/live-rig/` (research), so a label's ABSENT read is its start ledger holding no line of
that label. `WS`'s is its kept file's absence.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, not entries. Each reads «holds» only
when its case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line.

  refusal, stop where you are.
- The rig keeps its frames and the kept stamp locally; nothing of the operator's status line or config enters a

(leg=operator) as usual, and land `evidence/operator-pass.md`. Then stop: the wrap is a fresh window's.

body:
## 2026-11-19-a-fired-scheduled-wake-keeps-the-wheel — 11. A11y Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these): 1 row(s)
**Section:** 11. A11y Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these)
**Change:** ~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing · except: was «the test-only rig reads as closed words, never text: the trust selector's place, the input box as empty, holds-text or absent, modal dialogs, and after a turn end or send the box row's cell attributes»; now «the test-only rig reads closed words, never text: trust selector's place, the input box empty, holds-text or absent, modal dialogs, box-row cell attributes after a turn end or send or before any send»
**Why:** decision/no-screen-content-parsing: The live rig's HB arm reads the hint cells' attributes in a fresh box before any send, so the except gains that reading beside its standing members, each kept, the cell shortened to its bound. — resolved (Q1), PROVISIONAL: delegate the overseer, 2026-11-20: «Confirm all 12 (Recommended)» (PROVISIONAL; answer-card.md)
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-20T07-09-09Z-wrap/

- NEVER parse the rendered `claude` TUI beyond its compiled signatures (footer literals, the input box's rule and prompt rows, modal literals), the prompt row only for its opening char and never the text after it, or take screenshots as a11y evidence (R7); except the test-only rig, which reads as closed words, never text: the trust selector's place, the input box as empty, holds-text or absent, modal dialogs, and the box row's cell attributes after a turn end or send or before any send.

The only crate that knows Claude Code (test-only exceptions: the live rig in `viola-e2e` reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload and the cachedChromeExtensionInstalled key name, never a value, and its own captured StopFailure payload's key names, error word (one of the CLI's 13, else `other`) and two text lengths, never a text, and seeds its private Claude config; VH reads the real config's key names and a needle, never a value; the fake agent and the rig read a config's trust record). It parses hook payloads tolerantly and maps each hook to a normalised kind. It maps dialog answers to decision bodies (S3 / S7 / S8) and applies the R8 `CLAUDE*` strip. It resolves the child program (`resolve_program`: a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) and holds the Claude-specific half of the CLI version gate: the capability ledger rows (compiled) with their `viola verify` checks, `parse_version`, the stamp merge and `verified` verdict, and the fixture scrub. The gate's spawn is the root bin's `run::version_gate`; the stamps I/O is `viola_state::stamps`. It keeps the vt100 screen signatures (readiness gate), parses, in the pure `agents` module, a `claude agents --json` answer (`parse` into rows or a closed `AgentsFailure`, `oversize` · `malformed`; the read itself is the root bin's `run::agents`), and normalises `prompt-submitted` (removes the long-paste wrapper, then reverses tag escaping; classifies `origin` human/harness; the wrapper sets `driver` only on the in-flight send's own prompt and relabels a CLI-fired scheduled wake `harness`). It also holds the resume shapes `viola revive` launches with (`viola verify`'s Run E is the second caller of `resume_args(id, false)`): `PROGRAM` (`claude`), `RESUME_FLAG`, `FORK_SESSION_FLAG`, `is_session_id` (36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18, 23, ASCII hex elsewhere) and `resume_args(id, fork)`; it is the one product home of the two flag literals. It also holds the pure `marketplace` module, `viola plugin install`'s three documents built by `serde_json` (`marketplace_files`; `NAME` the marketplace `viola`, `PLUGIN_REF` `viola@viola`; its `.mcp.json` registers the MCP server `viola`, no hooks). No adapter trait yet: a second agent arrives as a sibling `viola-agent-<name>` crate, at which point the adapter trait is extracted into `viola-core`.

- Wheel / dialog rules as in arch: `send` during a running turn → `turn-running` (a send's post-gate section — the human-typing and turn-running reads, the link record, `send-issued` and the paste — runs under one wrapper flight lock that the `hook.event` claim, turn start and end and wheel moves also take, a human key never; the turn lives in memory in `WheelSlot` beside holder and cause: `append_hook_event` marks it on a `prompt-submitted` of any origin and ends it on `turn-ended` / `session-start` / `session-end` before the line is appended; only a `release` that returns a human-held wheel clears it; a human prompt takes the wheel, so the send after it reads `human-typing` — except, on a verified CLI, an unsent human-filed prompt with no key typed since the last human-filed prompt and a scheduled wake counted at the last turn end: a fired wake, relabelled `harness`, the wheel kept); `pause` → `manual-pause`; only CLI `release` returns the wheel; a pending dialog is answered `null` at once when the wheel moves to the human.

- **Wrapper:** `src/run/` (pump, wheel, gate wiring; `gate.rs` the bounded feed + `Gate`; `agents.rs` the bounded `claude agents --json` read (`read_logged`, `read_here`) shared by `list`, `revive`, verify's Run B and the `mcp` `list` tool (through `list::board_document`); `send.rs` the `send` module root — the `send` method on `Ctx` with its refusal order, re-exporting `SendSlot`, `append_hook_event` and `parse_from` —, one in flight with the remembered session id, the text validated as received and then typed with every inner CR or CR LF as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF (`typed_text`, the one text the list, the match, `text_bytes` and the paste read; an empty typed text is refused `empty-text` before the first wheel read, and by the client's `refusal_of` in `src/cmd/send.rs` before any frame), and its phases under `send/`: `slot.rs` the one-in-flight `SendSlot`, `append_hook_event` with the fired-wake relabel (a CLI-fired scheduled wake appended `origin:"harness"`, the wheel kept) and the driver relabel (a `prompt-submitted` that is the typed text, or a non-empty text equal to it less its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF, appended with `origin:"driver"`, its text kept as submitted) and the `session-start` post-condition claim, and for a stdout-echo local command its confirmation by counting `<local-command-stdout>` tags in the session transcript past its end recorded before the paste (only a count crosses, the read bounded by `MAX_FRAME`); `classify.rs` the local-command decision over `LOCAL_COMMANDS` (`classify`: a typed text exactly a listed name, or that name, one space and a non-empty rest not starting with a space, never by a leading slash); `params.rs` `parse` / `parse_from`; and beside `send.rs` in `src/run/`: `wait.rs` the `WaitFeed` — the append under its lock, the Condvar wake, the newest turn and its start rebuild (which also returns the highest `dialog_id`), `appending_dialog` / `dialog_settled` — and the `wait` / `last` methods; `dialog.rs` the `DialogSlot` — the `hook.dialog` and `answer` methods, one pending dialog, the Condvar await on the injected clock up to the instance's dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, a `DialogHold` of whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, read once at the wrapper's start through `run::dialog::read_hold`), at whose end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line (`{dialog_id, dialog_kind}`, `source: wrapper`) through `WaitFeed::appending`, waking a parked `wait`, the per-tool armed continuation matched on equal `tool_input`; `wheel.rs` the `WheelSlot` — holder + cause under one lock, the synchronous in-memory move, the record worker (the `wheel` event, the snapshot, `run.wheel_transition`, the pending-dialog hand-back) flushed ≤ 2 s at exit before the terminal leaves raw mode, the stdin observer `Observed` and the F-W2 `Classifier`, and the `pause` / `release` methods; `snapshot.rs` the `Snapshots` holder every snapshot write goes through)

- SessionStart → `session-start` (`cause` startup|clear|resume|compact|unknown, `agent_session_id`; the hook may send an optional string `transcript` param beside `event`, never inside it, only when the transcript path passes the shape check against its own session id; the wrapper re-validates it for a session-start line only, drops any other, and it never enters event data); UserPromptSubmit → `prompt-submitted` (`text` normalised: long-paste wrapper removed, then tag escaping reversed; `origin` driver|human|harness — the hook files only human|harness; the wrapper relabels a CLI-fired scheduled wake `harness`, and `driver` comes only from the wrapper's relabel of the in-flight send's own prompt, matched on the send's typed text, the sent text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters, or on a non-empty text equal to that typed text less its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF, the text kept as submitted); PreToolUse AskUserQuestion → `question`; PreToolUse ExitPlanMode → `plan`; PermissionRequest → `permission` (a PermissionRequest repeating the armed `question` / `plan` dialog's tool with an equal `tool_input` is that dialog's continuation and raises no event); Stop → `turn-ended` (`last_assistant_message` or `null`; `background_tasks`, the Stop payload's `background_tasks` array length, a count only, or `null` when the key is absent, `null` or not an array; `scheduled_wakes`, the Stop payload's `session_crons` array length, a count only, or `null` when the key is absent, `null` or not an array); StopFailure (`viola hook stop-failure`) → `turn-ended`, not a dialog (data exactly `last_assistant_message` null, `background_tasks` null, `scheduled_wakes` null and `cause` one of the nine `TurnEndCause` words, classified from the CLI's error word inside the Claude adapter); SessionEnd → `session-end`; Notification / PostToolUse / PostToolUseFailure → `activity`.

- Harness turns (a prompt whose raw start is `<agent-message from=`, `<task-notification>`, `<\cross-session-message` or `<cross-session-message`) are `origin:"harness"` and never flip the wheel. So is a fired scheduled wake: on a verified CLI, an unsent human-filed prompt with no key typed since the last human-filed prompt and a scheduled wake counted at the last turn end is relabelled `harness`, the wheel kept. The escaped cross-session form is the one escaped tag that classifies, so a human typing it at a prompt's start is filed `harness` (founder-ratified, 2026-09-29). As measured on 2.1.287, a human who types `<task-notification>` at a prompt's start is filed `harness` too.

- Disk state: the home's dirs 0700 and files 0600 set explicitly (the pinned binary 0700), the strict-modes check before any create, mode set or log open; only the wrapper writes `snapshot.json`, only `viola verify` writes `ledger/stamps.json` (save the test-only live rig, which seeds a stamp kept from its own verify scratch home into its own CC or R3W scratch home only); one write per ndjson line, atomic replace for the rest.

- NEVER answer `hook.dialog` non-`null` without a `viola verify` stamp read through `run`'s strict stamps read; only `viola verify` writes the stamps (the one exception: the test-only live rig seeds a stamp kept from its own verify scratch home into its own CC or R3W scratch home only). A stamp is read over the relied set (`LedgerRow::relied()`, on every build), so a decision flows only when every relied row counts: it reads pass, or absent on the browser-tools-prompt row alone (a stamp missing any other relied row or holding a failing one → `cli_verified:false`, `answer` exit 12; a stamp still holding the two retired status-line row ids reads on the relied rows alone); the founder's dated gap R2 is closed.

- Harness origin (Decisions Log `2026-09-29`, a boundary widening the founder ratified live): the compiled harness prefixes are four — `<agent-message from=`, `<task-notification>`, `<\cross-session-message`, `<cross-session-message` — matched on the prompt's raw start, and the wrapper relabels a keyless human-filed prompt told as a CLI-scheduled wake origin harness; the escaped cross-session form is the one escaped tag that classifies, so a human typing it at a prompt's start is filed `harness` (accepted side effect). As measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host (chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host) a real cross-session message arrived unescaped and was filed `harness` by the plain prefix, and a `<task-notification>` typed at a prompt's start arrives as typed, so it is filed `harness` too; the escaped injection form stays a relayed measurement and a compiled prefix. That reading and a names-only list of a 2.1.287 hook's `CLAUDE*` environment (12 names, four outside the 11-name floor, the floor unchanged) were two one-off scratch measurements on the founder's live answers of 2026-10-07T09:43Z, relayed by the overseer; neither answer covers a second message, a verify child or another probe.

- Test homes on the Linux dev host (the founder's live answer, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, relayed by the overseer; a boundary widening): `target/e2e-home` is a link to the per-user tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>`, so the fixture chain's sweep and drop and harness `cleanup` create and delete outside the working directory, each only a dir the test side itself made (by its owner record, its own temp dir or its session name prefix) or another build's stamp dir whose lock it takes with try_lock. The two keepers follow a linked base only when its target is absolute and one `lstat` reads a real directory with no group or other bit, and refuse a backing whose filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), each refusal a fixed message that names no path (the headroom one holds the two counts); they create it 0700 and remove nothing. `viola` never names the backing; no CI runner has the link. Accepted residual (a live round of `viola plugin install`): the round runs the CLI's own four commands (`claude plugin marketplace add` / `install` / `uninstall` / `marketplace remove`) at `--scope local`, a fresh count of four per rig, from a `proj/` that is its own git repo outside this work tree (on the e2e-home tmpfs, no ancestor `CLAUDE.md`): the CLI takes the local scope's project from the git work tree root, and a `proj/` inside the work tree meets the external-imports dialog after the trust dialog; the rig passes the folder-trust dialog by keys into its own pty only, never a desktop key, on the founder's own word anew for each chunk and by a closed argv grant (on a read screen at most 2 arrows toward the trust row and 1 Enter only when that row reads selected, one x and one DEL only in a ready box, any other key writing nothing; the founder's word binds the grant alone, and the rig's stop, Ctrl-C into its own pty or a no-key group kill, needs no word; on a wrapped start the keys move the wheel to the human, and `viola release <name>` precedes the driver's send); the CLI's writes are its own — its trust entry in `~/.claude.json` for each `proj/` whose dialog was accepted, the session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`, and after the removal its orphaned plugin cache `~/.claude/plugins/cache/viola/viola/<version>/` (re-written in place by a later install and uninstall), `installed_plugins.json` and `known_marketplaces.json` back as before (as measured on claude 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings); viola itself writes nothing under `~/.claude` or into `~/.claude.json`, save `viola verify`'s own trust record for its fresh temp folder in the Claude config its child reads, only that record removed after (a SIGKILL leaves it); on a verified CLI only, `run` and `revive`'s start set `hasTrustDialogAccepted` alone (every other key kept) in the trust record of an untrusted spawn folder in the config its child reads, never for the user home folder or a folder the CLI's own walk reads as trusted, and that record stays. Accepted residual (a scratch footer reading of a newer CLI): one `viola run` start of the CLI under a tmpfs `--home`, in a detached 80×24 pane, its cwd a fresh `.viola-footer-<pid>/` under the repository root, with no key typed; one `viola list` read against that home; at two instants the pane's bottom three screen rows, scrubbed of the home and the user word, written to the chunk's `evidence/`, never a row above the footer; then the start is killed and its cwd removed; it left no transcript under `~/.claude/projects/` (as measured on 2.1.302 at chunk 2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows). It is no product path and no standing permission: another such reading needs its own answer. The live rig runs its child under a private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in its own scratch, seeded only with keys whose values come from the CLI bundle's own logic, none read from the user's config (used-config markers and, on every arm but VP, the browser-tools prompt turned off; VP leaves the browser-tools key out), with an environment built from a closed kept list of host names plus its own, and reads the user's `~/.claude.json` only after a moved stamp, searching it for rig-made needles, dropping the bytes and keeping one closed word; the VH arm runs under the real home and config, reads no credentials, keeps only key names and one needle word, prints no value, and needs an explicit home, Claude dir and user config. The live rig may read whether the key name `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled` stands in its own private scratch config, printing written or absent, and never reads a value (a boundary widening, answered for the rig alone). The live rig's MCP recording arm keeps no CLI output (stdout drained and dropped, stderr kept only as a byte count and a SHA), and its MCP config is a private 0600 file inside the scratch, removed with it. The live rig's CX arm reads the session transcript through `MAX_FRAME`, counting only tags past the kept length and keeping no byte of it, and sends only through `viola send` under the rig's private config. A live session's screen frames are kept only under a gitignored local path, never in a work dir, a run dir or a commit; what lands is a closed-word summary per frame. The live rig copies the claude OAuth credentials file owner-only into its private scratch, reads only its expiry, refuses a start with under 20 minutes of token, removes the copy on every exit path, and writes no credential, host path or config value into any ledger, frame or summary; the VH arm, run under the real home, makes no copy and reads no credentials file. The live rig keeps a stamp from its CS or WS scratch home owner-only and no-clobber and seeds it only into its own CC or R3W scratch home; CC with no kept stamp refuses before its ledger line and before any scratch, R3W before its ledger line. The live rig's SF arm runs the real claude inside a network-closed bwrap sandbox with its own network namespace; an absent or failing sandbox, or one sharing the rig's namespace, refuses the arm with `refused: sandbox`, exit 3, uncounted, before any credentials read or ledger line. The live rig's R3W arm reads from the events log in its own scratch home only viola's own wheel lines and the prompt's origin word, and records the captured prompt's key names, never their values. The live rig's config-top reading keeps only the top-level names of its private claude config and their regular-file counts (a name outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,40}` reads as other) and reads no file content. The live rig's HB arm types one x and one DEL into a fresh box in its own unwrapped pty before any send, and records only cell attributes and counts, never screen text. The live rig's own hook capture (a ratified boundary widening) reads a payload under `MAX_FRAME` with the default JSON depth and writes one owner-only line: key names matching `[a-z_]{1,40}`, others counted; a UserPromptSubmit source word or a StopFailure error word of the CLI's 13, else `other`; two text lengths, never a text; a bad payload writes unread.

A SessionStart transcript path is accepted only when absolute, with no parent component, its file name exactly the payload's own session id plus `.jsonl` and that id of the closed session-id shape; the hook checks it and the wrapper re-checks it. In a hook payload each question's `option_details` keeps an option's `description` / `preview` only as strings (else `null`, never refusing the dialog), and the Stop's `background_tasks` is read as `IgnoredAny` elements and carried only as its length (`null` when absent, `null` or not an array), and its `session_crons` likewise only as its length, `scheduled_wakes` on turn-ended, which the wheel rule also reads; no element read or kept (`null` when absent, `null` or not an array, a non-array also writing one drift entry to the diagnostics detail file; `null` on an API-error turn end); a StopFailure's error text, `error_details` and `last_assistant_message` are dropped at the parse, its turn-ended data holding only `null` `last_assistant_message`, `background_tasks` and `scheduled_wakes` and one word of the closed nine-word turn-end cause set (crossing into `events.ndjson`, `wait --json` and MCP `wait`), and its error word is classified into one of those nine cause words inside the Claude adapter crate only, and only that cause word crosses out of the adapter, never the error word or any error text; the option text crossing into `events.ndjson`, `hook.dialog`, CLI `wait --json` and MCP `wait` is a boundary widening the founder answered himself (P4 fork Q4 of chunk 2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola). Standing as `hyprctl` by its own file name (in a test-scoped bin dir, in place of the real `hyprctl`; viola-hyprland's own unit tests serve `hyprctl` by a planted shell stub instead, because cargo-mutants runs only the mutated package's tests, so a root-package test cannot kill that crate's mutants), it reads its mode and reply set from files beside its exe, never from the env. A non-absolute command is receipted `command_absolute:false, ran:false` and never run. The payload is `<fixtures>/<cli-version>/<Event>.<variant>.json`, with only `prompt` set for UserPromptSubmit and the fixture's trailing newline kept, so the recorded prompt yields the recorded bytes; under `--resume <id>` the launch SessionStart is the set's recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` when the set holds it, else its recorded `SessionStart.default` (a set without the variant), with `source` `resume` and `session_id` the id given (with `--fork-session`, the compiled fork id), and no other payload is built save the compact replay's `SessionStart.compact-1` under `--framing`, whose `session_id` is set to the last SessionStart the agent fired, under `--transcript` the launch SessionStart's `transcript_path`, and under `--stop-crons` each Stop's `session_crons`.

- Run start's span chain is `run.start` (INTERNAL, root) › `state.snapshot_recover` › `run.collision_check` › `run.pin_copy` › `run.version_gate` › `channel.bind` › `state.snapshot_write` › `state.heartbeat_start` › `pty.spawn` (CLIENT), with no budget span. The wrapper's stdin typed mark and its held scheduled-wakes count are in-memory state that open no span and write no line of their own, and carry no key and no prompt text. A `send-refused` line carries `refusal`, `detail`, `side` and `wheel`, never `window`, `used_percentage`, `resets_at` or `paused`. At a dialog hold's end (`run.dialog_await`'s `deadline_ms`, `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s` in ms, 60 000–3 600 000, default 60 000) the wrapper appends one `dialog-expired{dialog_id, dialog_kind}` product line and writes one `dialog-answered{corr:<dialog_id>, dialog_kind, deadline_hit:true, duration_ms}` with no `from` / `from_trust`; a hand-back or an answer writes neither; the hook then writes `hook-decision{decision_emitted:false, deadline_hit:false}`, `deadline_hit:true` only when its own read times out at its backstop bound `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s).
